panels.description: Every webhook send attempt that reached the channel adapter, classified. 'success' = 2xx; 'transient' = retryable (5xx, 429, network/timeout); 'permanent' = not retried (4xx, auth misconfiguration). Suppressed windows never reach the adapter and so do not appear here.
panels.title: Send attempts by outcome

panels.description: The diagnostic panel: where delivery is failing and why. `stage` is the leg of send() the attempt ended in. stage=auth means token acquisition failed and the webhook POST was never issued — status_class then describes the AUTH server, so auth/timeout is 'could not reach the auth server' (bad tokenUrl, DNS, timeout) while auth/4xx_other is 'the auth server rejected our credentials'. stage=delivery is the webhook POST itself: 5xx = the receiver is down, timeout = unreachable, 401 = their OAuth credential or token endpoint is broken, 403 = valid but not authorised, 429 = they are throttling us. stage=validation means the stored webhook URL failed the send-time SSRF re-check and nothing was sent. stage=unknown means an adapter returned no stage — an instrumentation bug on our side, not a customer problem. Note a server-sent 408 carries an httpStatus and so lands in 4xx_other, not timeout.
panels.title: Failed attempts by stage & status class

panels.description: The complete loss picture — two distinct modes that no single metric covers. give_up{max_attempts} = transient failures exhausted MAX_ATTEMPTS; give_up{permanent} = a 4xx or misconfiguration, never retried; orphaned = the meta key expired before its fireAt was reached, so the notification was dropped before any send was attempted (usually a per-endpoint Max Delay configured longer than the ~20 min arm-key TTL). Orphans carry no org/project labels — the meta that held them is gone.
panels.title: Notifications lost
